architecture_decisions: {architecture_decision: "Implement a provider-neutral, configuration-driven local-first model routing capability for Parallax instances"}
validations: {validation: "Ensure local-first routing is opt-in and server-owned"}

AC-01: validate protected requirement — `P2-V0.19.8` is the only specification/evidence identity for the reconciled local-first candidate. Current authoritative `P2-V0.19.7` remains byte-for-byte owned by Wave 6 and is not replaced or reinterpreted.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — With no admitted local-first configuration, effective runtime order remains exactly Luna -> Terra -> Sol and existing hosted transport/routing tests remain green.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — One bounded server-owned local route can precede the hosted chain outside Vercel production. Empty, duplicate, malformed, unsupported, caller-controlled, secret-bearing or reserved-credential configuration fails closed before model execution.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — When `VERCEL_ENV=production`, enabling local-first routing fails closed before any local endpoint request, whether the endpoint is loopback or remote HTTPS. The accepted hosted chain remains the only automatic production route under this workstream.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — A configured local endpoint applies only to its exact admitted local model. Hosted GPT-5.6 routes continue to use the fixed Vercel AI Gateway with canonical model IDs and cannot be redirected to the local endpoint.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Outside Vercel production, when the local route returns a result accepted by the existing protected validator, routing returns that result and does not attempt a hosted model.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Outside Vercel production, local unavailability/provider failure records only bounded sanitized evidence and advances to the next admitted hosted route without changing acceptance requirements.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — When the local route returns output rejected by the existing protected validator, routing records `validation_failed`, advances to the next admitted route and cannot lower or bypass the validator.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Request-scoped Vercel OIDC remains the only automatic hosted-production GPT-5.6 credential path. Process `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, local credentials and local configuration cannot substitute for hosted-production authority.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Existing explicit `DSPY_API_BASE` / `DSPY_API_KEY` behavior remains a deliberate whole-transport operator/development override. Local-first configuration is disabled rather than silently combined when that explicit override is present.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Logs and attempt evidence contain only admitted model/provider identity, status, duration and sanitized error class. Tests prove endpoint credentials, authorization values, raw exception text/results, prompts and generated content are absent.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Tests and code inspection prove local-first routing grants no source acceptance, Project/spec mutation, shell/filesystem authority, unrestricted network capability, provider spending/administration, GitHub/Vercel authority, approval, REVIEW completion or production deployment authority.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — The semantic candidate is constructed from the current reconciled `main` lineage rather than by directly merging old PR #303. Wave 6 runtime/replay, model transport, safe deletion and current whole-product tests remain green.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — DSPy SpecCritic + SpecCompiler execute authentically for `P2-V0.19.8`; protected `--require-dspy` validation passes; the final exact candidate passes applicable Workstream Spec Validation, Bounded Autonomy Pilot and P2 CI before it is considered ready for integration review.

AC-15: validate protected requirement — This candidate stops ready for integration review. No merge to `main`, production configuration change or deployment occurs until Control Tower explicitly authorizes integration and a governed release verifies the exact accepted head.
risks: {risk: "Potential security risks if local-first routing is not properly configured"}
